text:
alex: Heads-up — PMs pushed a set of customer asks around geo+tenant isolation. want to map tradeoffs before we bake into the roadmap.
maria: can you paste the asks?
alex: Short list: 1) per-tenant regional pinning (data residency) 2) hard isolation lanes for higher SLA customers 3) graceful fallback to lower-cost model variants across regions
sam: + a request for explicit billing boundaries when traffic crosses regions (legal asked).
jordan: we should avoid a single monolithic solution — propose 3 patterns: territory lanes, soft-routing with data tags, and tenant-tunnels.
anya: quick defs?
jordan: territory lanes = strict host pool per geo/tenant. soft-routing = preferred region but allow failover. tenant-tunnels = customer-owned private path/vpc to specific capacity.
maria: what are the main tradeoffs? latency/cost/ops complexity?
alex: yep. territory lanes = best for compliance and SLAs but highest cost. soft-routing = cheaper but harder to guarantee residency. tunnels = heavy infra and onboarding.
sam: customers care about predictability + contractability. they want SLA + clear migration path.
anya: launch criteria suggestion: 1) define policy DSL + templates, 2) telemetry for cross-region egress cost, 3) e2e test harness for failover scenarios, 4) legal signoff on residency guarantees.
maria: can we reuse existing routing policy engine or we need new surface?
jordan: reuse core + add "territory" policy layer that maps tenants -> lane. minimal API change: new enum in route config: { "territory":"strict|preferred|tunnel" }
alex: sample config snippet: ```json
{
  "tenant": "acme",
  "territory": "strict",
  "primary_region": "us-west-2",
  "fallback_policy": "none"
}
```
sam: important: fallback_policy must be explicit for strict lanes (deny vs degrade).
anya: ops question: how do we surface capacity constraints during canary/cutover? need admission control + customer-facing ETA.
maria: also requires product decision on billable egress and reserved capacity pricing.
jordan: technical debt callout: KV cache locality — strict lanes need cache warm-up per lane; adds memory overhead.
alex: action items: - draft policy DSL PR (jordan) - run cost model for strict vs preferred (sam) - prod legal checklist (maria) - define canary/cutover playbook + telemetry (anya)
maria: timeline proposal: prototype DSL + model in Q2, internal pilot Q3, public beta Q4.
anya: small experiment: pick 1 mid-size customer and run soft->strict migration to measure cost & latency delta.
sam: note: include billing/contract templates in pilot so sales can offer clear T&Cs.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: routing-policy-prototype branch -> staging at 2026-06-12T09:00Z :rocket:
alex: ok team — let's sync tomorrow 10am PT, bring short exec summary for PM+Sales. :thumbsup:
